title: epochal soft-fuse and backfill for tenant-model fallbacks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We need a tenant-aware circuit breaker that trips conservatively for high-importance tenants but can still protect overall SLOs by gracefully degrading to cheaper model variants or cached responses. Existing single-threshold breakers are too coarse: tenants with bursty traffic or longer KV-cache warmups either trip too often or push the system past latency/queueing SLOs.

Proposal: Implement an 'epochal soft-fuse' breaker per (tenant, model, dependency) that adjusts trip sensitivity across short-lived epochs and supports staged backfill strategies. Key ideas: 1) epoch windows (e.g., 10s) compute short-term indicators (p95 latency, queue depth, error rate); 2) soft thresholding uses a two-stage decision (warn -> bounded-shed -> hard-trip) with hysteresis; 3) temporal backfill / backoff where traffic is routed to compatible, lower-cost model variants (quantized/shorter-context) or served from prefix cache; 4) conditional epochal retries that allow limited sampling to the primary model to avoid regression blindspots; 5) per-tenant weight scaling so high-SLA tenants get larger grace but still honor cluster-wide SLOs; 6) multi-region failover hooks to prefer local region until sustained degradation triggers cross-region reroute.

Why different from existing work: Unlike single-trip, coarse breakers, the epochal soft-fuse provides gradual degradation with observable phases and a deterministic backfill plan. It explicitly ties trip behavior to SLO buckets (latency vs correctness) and includes sampling/retry to detect recovery without full re-enable risk.

Design artifacts: Confluence spec (link below) with state machine diagrams, metric math for epoch thresholds, and compatibility matrix for model fallbacks. Implementation will be split: runtime changes (metrics windowing, per-path breaker state), routing layer changes (backfill policy and variant catalog lookup), and console UI changes (per-tenant breaker view, historical epoch traces).

Rollout plan: feature-flagged by tenant and region; start in canary region with low-impact tenants, enable telemetry (decision_events, epoch_traces) and a dashboard. Gradual widening to higher-tenancy groups after 2-week observation and SLO validation.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes epoch-based indicator stream (10s windows) for p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, and error rate per (tenant, model)
Breaker implements three visible states with hysteresis: OK, BoundedShed (probabilistic routing + backfill), HardTrip (full backfill + rate limit)
Backfill policy supports routing to compatible model variants, prefix-cache, and deterministic fallbacks with per-tenant weighting
Conditional epochal retry mechanism allows 0.1%-1% sampled requests to primary model while in BoundedShed, with circuit reopen logic on sustained success
Multi-region trigger rules documented and tested: local region degradation -> prioritized cross-region failover after sustained epochs without recovery
Console shows per-tenant epoch_traces and decision_events and allows temporary manual override and rollback
Integration tests cover regression scenarios: slow KV warmup, cold-start for model shard, and tenant burst at 10x baseline
Canary roll validated for 14 days without increased global SLO violations (no more than 0.5% delta)
comments: 2026-02-18 Ava Chen: Created ticket and initial proposal. Added links to spec and early simulation results. Suggest splitting work into runtime + routing + console sub-tasks.

2026-02-22 Miguel Ortiz: Spike complete. Implemented epoch window aggregator prototype in the local dev branch. Observed reduced oscillation vs 30s single-window test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1023

2026-02-25 Priya Patel (SRE): Reviewed approach. Request: add quota guard for sampled conditional retries to avoid accidental amplification. Also asked for explicit metrics for 'backfill fidelity' to measure semantic regression risk.

2026-03-01 Design review (Liam Wong): Reviewed UI flows for per-tenant breaker control. Suggested adding timeline scrubber for epoch traces and a compact view for on-call. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/epochal-soft-fuse

2026-03-04 Miguel Ortiz: Implemented the two-stage decision machine and integrated deterministic backfill lookup. Added feature flag 'epochal_soft_fuse_v1' guarded by tenant list. Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1047

2026-03-07 Test lead (Anika Rao): Started integration tests against synthetic workloads. Found edge-case where per-tenant weight scaling allowed a small number of tenants to exceed node-level queue SLOs; mitigation: add cluster-level adjustment factor and a hard capacity cap per-node.
2026-03-10 Miguel Ortiz: Mitigation implemented. Updated thresholds and added circuit-level capacity cap. Preparing canary rollout to eu-west-1 with 12 low-risk tenants on 2026-03-12.
2026-03-10 Ava Chen: Marked ticket In Progress -> pending canary results. Next steps: observe epoch_traces, validate backfill fidelity metrics, capture any customer-impacting anomalies.
